## **Understanding Colorado Springs Medical Records: Your Essential Guide for PI Lawyers**


### **Why Medical Records Are Critical in Personal Injury Cases**


Medical records document the connection between the incident and the injuries, establish treatment timelines, and quantify damages. Incomplete records create gaps defense attorneys exploit, and delays postpone case evaluation and client compensation.


Most Colorado Springs cases involve several providers: emergency departments, specialists, physical therapists, and imaging centers. Each keeps separate records with its own procedures and timelines, and managing those by hand burns paralegal hours that should go into case strategy.


### **The Colorado Medical Records Landscape**


Three major systems shape Colorado Springs healthcare:


-


UCHealth Memorial operates Memorial Hospital Central, Memorial Hospital North, Pikes Peak Regional Hospital, and Grandview Hospital


-


CommonSpirit runs Penrose Hospital and St. Francis Medical Center


-


Children's Hospital Colorado operates southern Colorado's first pediatric-only hospital and the region's dedicated pediatric emergency department


Knowing which system treated your client determines where requests go and which forms apply. Codes Health reaches records through claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone outreach, which helps when a case spans several facilities or a client cannot recall every provider.


## **HIPAA Authorization Forms: The Foundation for Medical Record Requests**


### **Key Elements of a Valid HIPAA Authorization**


Under[45 CFR § 164.508](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.508) , a valid authorization generally has to include:


-


A description of the information to be disclosed, identified in a specific and meaningful way


-


Who may make the disclosure, meaning the facility or department


-


Who may receive it, meaning your firm and the attorney of record


-


The purpose, which may read "at the request of the individual" when the patient initiates it


-


An expiration date or event, such as resolution of the legal claim


-


The individual's signature and date, plus a representative's authority if someone signs on the patient's behalf


-


Required statements on the right to revoke in writing, conditioning of treatment, payment, enrollment, or benefits, and the possibility that redisclosed information loses HIPAA protection


Facilities routinely ask for more than the rule requires. A date of birth, address, partial Social Security number, or photo ID may be part of a provider's identity-verification process; UCHealth asks for photo ID with authorizations submitted outside My Health Connection. Those are facility requirements, not federal ones.


### **Common Pitfalls to Avoid with HIPAA Forms**


Incomplete or defective authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can send a request straight back and restart the provider's processing clock. Common errors include:


-


A missing signature, or one that fails the facility's identity-verification step


-


Record descriptions so broad the facility asks for more specificity, where targeted date ranges would have moved things along


-


Absent expiration dates or events


-


Unchecked boxes for sensitive records including mental health, substance use, or HIV/AIDS


-


The wrong facility name when systems share similar names


[Codes Health's AI review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) validates authorizations before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


## **Requesting Medical Records: Forms and Procedures for Colorado Springs Facilities**

UCHealth directs Southern Colorado release of information mail and drop-off to the Memorial Administrative Center, but also publishes facility-specific contacts and asks requesters to name the exact locations they need.


**Contact Information:**

-

-

-

**Processing Time:** UCHealth says most My Health Connection requests are fulfilled within 48 to 72 hours, while other record requests may take up to 30 business days. Do not assume that shorter window covers a comprehensive attorney request.


**Authorization Form:** Available through UCHealth's[medical records page](https://www.uchealth.org/access-my-health-connection/medical-records-uchealth) . One form covers Memorial Central, Memorial North, Pikes Peak Regional, and Grandview. Spanish language assistance: 844-945-2500.

**Children's Hospital Colorado Consent Requirements:**

**Authorization Forms:** The Patient Request for Access to PHI form is on the hospital's[medical records page](https://www.childrenscolorado.org/your-visit/medical-records/) . A separate HIPAA authorization form is required for third-party requests, including attorney requests. Fax numbers differ by form and location, so use the number printed on the current form.

## **Getting Your Old Medical Records: Strategies for PI Cases**


### **Tracing Your Client's Medical History**


Long-term injury cases reach back years or decades, complicated by closed facilities, provider retirements, system mergers, and incomplete client recollection of treatment locations.


The **Colorado State Archives** may hold records where a government institution's files or a historical collection were transferred there. It is not a general repository for charts from closed private practices, so identify the former facility's custodian or successor first. Requests go through[archives.colorado.gov](https://archives.colorado.gov/request) ; confirm current hours, fees, and appointment rules before relying on them.


**Records destruction notice:** Intermountain Health, formerly SCL Health, announced that qualifying older paper records from Lutheran Medical Center, St. Joseph Hospital, and Platte Valley Hospital would begin being destroyed April 1, 2026, with a stated request deadline of March 30, 2026. That deadline has passed, so confirm current availability directly with Intermountain.


### **Colorado Retention Requirements**


Colorado retention periods vary by facility type and profession. Some facility regulations call for ten years for adult records and the period of minority plus ten years for minors, while other rules and board policies use different periods; chiropractic and dental rules each follow their own schedule. Check the rule governing the specific provider rather than assuming one statewide standard, and request imaging promptly when a case turns on it.

## **Ensuring Completeness and Accuracy: The Missing Piece in Medical Record Retrieval**


### **Why Complete Records Matter**


Partial record sets let defense counsel argue treatment gaps, question causation, or imply undisclosed pre-existing conditions. Commonly missing elements include:


-


Physician progress notes and consulting physician notes


-


Radiology images where only reports arrived


-


Nursing notes and flow sheets


-


Billing records and itemized statements


### **Completeness Verification**


Codes Health checks delivered records against the original request before closing a retrieval, and works with the facility to resolve gaps before returning the set. That turns the deliverable from a stack of documents into a record set someone has verified.


Speed claims deserve the same scrutiny. Codes Health notes that services promising same-day retrieval typically return only what is immediately available electronically, leaving the firm or client to chase the rest, and it says that added client involvement is a common driver of churn.


## **Personal Injury Lawyer's Checklist for Colorado Springs Medical Record Requests**


### **Step-by-Step Request Process**


**Step 1: Obtain Client Authorization**


-


Include every required HIPAA element


-


Add special consent initials for sensitive records


-


Meet the facility's identity-verification requirements


-


Set an appropriate expiration date or event


**Step 2: Submit Through the Facility's Preferred Channel**


-


Use the online form, portal, fax, email, or mail the facility prefers


-


Include a cover letter specifying exact date ranges and record types


-


Request electronic format, which Colorado requires when records are electronically stored and readily producible


**Step 3: Pay Applicable Fees** Colorado's page-based schedule under C.R.S. § 25-1-801:


-


First 10 pages: $18.53


-


Pages 11 to 40: $0.85 per page


-


Pages 41 and beyond: $0.57 per page


-


Microfilm: $1.50 per page


-


Certification: $10 if requested


For qualifying attorney requests, HB26-1414, effective August 12, 2026, caps requests exceeding 664 pages at $400, subject to exceptions, and adds invoice, timing, and electronic-delivery rules. Confirm which schedule applies before approving an invoice.


**Step 4: Track and Follow Up**


-


Confirm receipt if no acknowledgment arrives in the first week


-


Send a status inquiry at the facility's stated turnaround


-


Escalate in writing under the rule that governs your request: the federal right-of-access standard, Colorado's timing provisions, or facility policy


**Step 5: Review and Supplement**


-


Compare received records against the facility's medical record index


-


Verify date ranges match the request


-


Submit supplemental requests for missing elements


### **Common Mistakes to Avoid**


-


Sending requests to the wrong facility within a health system


-


Using broad record descriptions where specific date ranges would speed processing


-


Failing to account for 42 CFR Part 2 when requesting records from a federally assisted substance use disorder program


-


Missing minor patient signatures for protected record types where facilities require them


-


Accepting partial releases without comparing them against the request

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What happens if a Colorado facility exceeds the statutory fee limits?**


Colorado sets maximum fees that facilities cannot exceed, and HB26-1414 adds a cap for qualifying attorney requests over 664 pages as of August 12, 2026. If an invoice looks too high, respond in writing, cite the provision you believe applies, and request a corrected invoice. Raise unresolved disputes with the provider and document them for potential cost recovery in litigation.


### **Can I subpoena medical records instead of using authorization forms?**


Subpoena availability depends on an existing proceeding and the procedural authority behind it, so authorization-based requests are the common tool during pre-litigation investigation. HIPAA does permit disclosure in response to a subpoena without a court order when the conditions in 45 CFR § 164.512(e) are met, such as adequate notice to the individual or reasonable efforts to secure a qualified protective order. Facilities may add their own procedures, but those are policy rather than the federal rule.


### **How do I obtain records from a provider who has retired or closed their practice?**


Colorado licensing-board rules may impose notice, retention, transfer, or custodial requirements when a practice closes, and those rules vary by profession. Start with the former practice, any successor organization, the provider's liability carrier, or a designated custodian, and check the relevant board's rules. Boards can point you toward guidance but do not hold the records themselves. Some records may already have been destroyed under retention rules, so document your retrieval attempts.


### **What are my options if a facility denies my medical records request?**


Request a written explanation citing the basis for denial, then contact the facility's designated HIPAA privacy official. If that fails, an access-rights complaint can be filed with the HHS Office for Civil Rights through ocrportal.hhs.gov. In active litigation, a motion to compel or subpoena duces tecum may be appropriate. Keep all correspondence for the case file and any later proceedings.


### **Do Colorado medical records laws differ from federal HIPAA regulations?**


Yes. C.R.S. § 25-1-801 and related provisions add protections beyond HIPAA minimums, including fee caps and electronic-format production when records are electronically stored and readily producible. HB26-1414, effective August 12, 2026, layers additional cost, invoice, and timing rules onto qualifying attorney requests. Where state and federal law differ, the more protective provision applies, and Colorado's minor-consent provisions reach further than HIPAA for certain record types.
